title: Holidays — Create / Edit
overviewHtml: A named public holiday in a holiday calendar — Eid al-Fitr, National Day. Its actual dates each year are entered as holiday periods.

fields.label: Code
fields.rules: Optional. Left blank, the next number is assigned when the record is saved. Must be unique in this list.
fields.html:
What it is. A short code that identifies this item in its list.

Example. 001

fields.label: NameEn
fields.rules: Required. Must be unique in this list.
fields.html: What it is. The item's name in English.

fields.label: NameAr
fields.rules: Required. Must be unique in this list.
fields.html: What it is. The item's name in Arabic.

fields.label: HolidayCalendar
fields.rules: Required. Chosen from Holiday Calendar master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The calendar the holiday belongs to.

Example. Kuwait Public Holidays

fields.label: OvertimeType
fields.rules: Optional. Chosen from Overtime Type master data.
fields.html:
What it is. The overtime type for work done on this holiday.

Example. Holiday Overtime

Why it matters. On the holiday, overtime is recorded under this type instead of the duty's.
fields.adminHtml: The holiday is found by date only, not through the employee's own holiday calendar. If holidays in two calendars share a date, one of their overtime types is used for everyone — give them the same overtime type. Legacy behaviour, kept on purpose.
